name: Refract – AI Social Media Scheduler for Blog Posts
author: anpsthemes

sections.description:
Refract shares every blog post you publish to Bluesky, Mastodon, Pinterest, Telegram and the other networks you connect, with a version written for each network in your voice. You approve each version in the post editor or in Refract, and Refract posts it.

When you publish a post, Refract gets it as a note. It writes a version for each account you chose, in your workspace’s voice, and crops the post’s images for each network. Every version waits for your approval. You preview and approve the versions in the post editor, or in Refract. Nothing goes out until you approve it.

Bring readers back from social

Each version links back to your post, so your blog gets visits and your links get shared. Once a version is posted, the post editor shows the link to it and the clicks so far, for example “12 clicks from Bluesky”.

From WordPress to Refract

  • Send posts when they’re published, or only when you choose, from the editor.
  • Choose the post types, the categories and the accounts.
  • See each version in the post sidebar: its text, its image in the network’s shape and its status.
  • Approve each version, or approve all and add them to the queue. Or open one in Refract to edit it.
  • Works with the block editor and the Classic Editor plugin.

From Refract to WordPress

Your site becomes an account in Refract. From Refract you can send blog posts to it as drafts, or, if you allow it, publish or schedule them. Refract can create posts, update the posts it created and move them to the trash. It can’t change anything else on your site: not other posts, settings, users, plugins, themes or files. It’s off until you turn it on, and then sends drafts only unless you choose otherwise. You choose which user the posts show as their author (Refract never signs in as that user) and the default category. You can turn this off at any time.

Link previews

The plugin can add social preview tags (Open Graph and X card), so your links show a title and an image on every network. If another plugin already adds these tags, the plugin leaves them to it.

Networks

Networks you can connect: TikTok, YouTube, X, Pinterest, Bluesky, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Tumblr, Slack, Pixelfed and DEV.

Coming soon: Instagram, Facebook, Threads, LinkedIn, Google Business Profile and Lemmy.

What you need

  • A Refract account. You can start with a free trial at refract.social, no card needed.
  • AI credits for the versions. Each version costs 1 AI credit, and your plan includes credits each month. With your own AI key in Refract, versions cost no credits. You can also send the same post, with the link, to every account for free.
  • WordPress 6.8 or later and PHP 8.1 or later. Multisite works: each site connects separately.

Source code

The JavaScript in build/ is made with @wordpress/scripts. Its unminified source is in the plugin’s src/ folder, and the build setup is in package.json and webpack.config.js. To build it yourself, run npm install and then npm run build in the plugin’s folder. The source code is also on GitHub: anpsthemes-wp-themes/refract-for-wordpress.

The network icons in src/common/marks.js come from Simple Icons (CC0 1.0). The Refract mark, and the network marks Simple Icons doesn’t have, are drawn for this plugin.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Refract (https://refract.social), a service that writes social posts from your blog posts and schedules them. You need a Refract account to use it. Nothing is sent to Refract until you click “Connect to Refract”.

What’s sent, and when:

  • When you connect: your site’s name and address, the versions of WordPress and of the plugin, the site’s language and time zone, and a signing secret the plugin makes, so Refract can sign what it sends to your site.
  • When Refract asks what your site looks like (when you connect, and when someone writes a post for your site in Refract; Refract keeps the answer for 10 minutes): your site’s name and address, the versions of WordPress and of the plugin, the site’s language and time zone, its categories and up to 200 tags, the default category, and the display name of the person Refract publishes as.
  • When a post is sent to Refract, after you publish it or click “Send to Refract”: the post’s title, excerpt, text, link and images (with their alt text), and the accounts chosen for it. Updates to the post are sent the same way, unless you turn that off.
  • When a post you sent stops being public, or is public again (published, draft, pending, private, scheduled, password-protected, in the trash or deleted): the post’s ID in Refract and that status.
  • When the post sidebar loads its versions: the post’s ID in Refract. When you approve versions, which ones you approved.
  • When you disconnect or delete the plugin: a request to end the connection.
  • When the post sidebar or the Classic Editor box shows a version’s image: your browser loads the image from Refract’s media host (https://media.refract.social).
  • When Refract publishes a post on your site: your site downloads the post’s images from Refract’s media host (https://media.refract.social) and adds them to your media library.

Refract also sends requests to your site: it downloads the post’s images from their links, sends updates about your versions, and, if you allow it, creates posts (drafts unless you choose otherwise), updates the posts it created or moves them to the trash.

Refract’s terms of service: https://refract.social/legal/terms
Refract’s privacy policy: https://refract.social/legal/privacy
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins › Add New, search for “Refract” and click Install, then Activate. Or upload the plugin’s folder to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate it on the Plugins screen.
  2. Go to Refract › Settings and click “Connect to Refract”. Sign in to Refract, or start a free trial, and allow the connection.
  3. Choose the workspace, the accounts that get a version of each post, and when to send posts to Refract. Click Save.

If the redirect back to your site doesn’t work, for example on a local site or a site behind a login, open “Connect with a token instead”. Create a token in Refract under Settings › API and agents, and paste it there.
sections.faq:
Does it post without my approval?

No. Every version waits for your OK. You approve it in the post editor’s Refract panel or in Refract, and only then does Refract add it to your queue. Sending a post to Refract when you publish only starts the writing: nothing is posted until you approve it.

Which networks can it post to?

The networks listed under Networks above. Networks marked Coming soon can’t be connected yet. The list is also at refract.social/wordpress-plugin.

Is it free?

The plugin is free. Refract is a paid service, with a free trial and no card needed. Each version costs 1 AI credit, and your plan includes credits each month; with your own AI key in Refract, versions cost no credits. Sending the same post, with the link, to every account is always free. If you run out of credits, the post sidebar tells you, and you can send the same post to every account instead.

Does it work with the block editor and the Classic Editor?

Yes. In the block editor, Refract is a panel in the sidebar. With the Classic Editor plugin, it’s a box next to your post. Both show each version with its text, its image in the network’s shape and its status, with Approve and Edit in Refract.

Will it slow my site down?

No. It adds no scripts or styles to the pages your visitors see. Posts go to Refract in the background, through WP-Cron, a few seconds after you publish, so publishing doesn’t wait for Refract. On your pages it only adds social preview tags (Open Graph and X card), and only when no SEO plugin adds them already; you can turn them off. For those previews it also keeps a 1200 × 630 copy of each image you upload.

Can Refract publish to my WordPress site?

Yes, if you turn on “Let Refract publish to this site” in the plugin’s settings. It then sends drafts only, unless you choose “Publish and schedule posts”. Refract can create posts, update the posts it created and move them to the trash; it can’t change anything else on your site. You choose which user the posts show as their author, and the default category. Posts that come from Refract are never sent back to Refract.

Do I need a Refract account?

Yes. The plugin connects your site to Refract, which writes the versions and schedules the posts. You can start with a free trial.

What is sent to Refract, and when?

Nothing, until you click Connect. The External services section below lists what’s sent and when.

Can I change a version before it’s posted?

Yes. Click “Edit in Refract” on the version to open it in Refract.

What happens when I update a post that was already sent?

By default, Refract updates the note when the title, excerpt or text changes, and writes again the versions nobody edited. Those versions, and the ones someone edited, need approval again before the post goes out, even if it was already scheduled, and the people who approve are told at once. If you choose “Leave it” under “When the post changes after it was sent”, changes aren’t sent: versions already approved go out as they are, even if the post changed.

What happens if I change or unpublish a post after approving its versions?

A change to the title, excerpt or text works as in the answer above. Images, the slug on its own and the accounts picked for the post aren’t sent after the first send. If you move the post to draft, pending, private or scheduled, add a password, move it to the trash or delete it, Refract holds its post at once, so nothing goes out with a link readers can’t open, and the team is told. When the post is public again, its versions need approval again in Refract before it goes out. This happens whatever you chose for “When the post changes after it was sent”.

Does it work with multisite?

Yes. Network activation works, and each site connects to Refract separately.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating stops the plugin’s scheduled tasks and keeps the connection. Deleting the plugin removes its settings and post data, and asks Refract to end the connection.
sections.changelog:
1.2.3

  • When a post you sent stops being public (draft, pending, private, scheduled, password-protected, in the trash or deleted), Refract holds it, so no version goes out with a link readers can’t open, and tells your team. When the post is public again, its versions need approval again.
  • A post published again after being unpublished sends its changes, when updates are on.
  • The post panel says when Refract is holding a post, and the Activity log lists it.
  • The settings say what “Leave it” means: versions already approved go out as they are.

1.2.2

  • A clearer name and description in the plugin directory: “Refract – AI Social Media Scheduler for Blog Posts”.
  • New screenshots, with accounts on networks you can connect today.
  • No change to how the plugin works.

1.2.1

  • Publishing from Refract never acts as a user on your site. The “Publish as” person is only shown as the author, and what they can do is checked before anything changes.
  • Publishing from Refract sends drafts only until you choose “Publish and schedule posts”.
  • The settings page says exactly what Refract can and can’t do on your site.

1.2.0

  • A clearer Settings page: the connection at the top, a section for each part (Sending, Accounts, Writing and images, Publishing from Refract, Link previews) with a summary of what’s chosen, and links to jump between them.
  • Choices are cards that say what each one does, and which ones use AI credits or are free.
  • Accounts show as cards by network, with how many are chosen and Select all or Select none. Pick categories by searching for them.
  • Save changes stays in view while you have unsaved changes, with Discard changes. Leaving the page asks first.
  • Settings and Activity are tabs at the top of both pages.

1.1.0

  • Refract can remove a post it published on your site: when you remove the post in Refract, it moves to the trash here.

1.0.0

  • First release: connect your site, send posts to Refract, preview and approve the versions in the editor, publish from Refract to your site, social preview tags and the Activity log.
